title: Uncomputability of the halting function
statement: For every effective machine representation scheme $c$, no finite-state Boolean Turing machine computes the function sending each bit string $s$ to the one-bit string whose bit is the value of the halting function of $c$ at $s$.
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective coding scheme for Turing machines, i.e.\ one admitting a
universal evaluator machine, and let $\mathrm{HALT}_c$ be its halting function:
true on a bit string $s$ exactly when $s$ is the pairing encoding
$\langle \alpha, x \rangle$ of two bit strings and the machine denoted by
$\alpha$ under $c$ produces some output on input $x$ within some finite number of
steps, and false otherwise. Then no Turing machine computes the function mapping
$s$ to the one-bit string carrying $\mathrm{HALT}_c(s)$ [AB09, Theorem 1.11].
